title: Analysis of the Compound Impact of Antecedent Dry Spell and Rainstorm Events on Urban Surface Water Quality
content:
ABSTRACT

Urban runoff is a key factor in the deteriorating ecological state of urban water bodies. Longer dry spells followed by heavy rains (cascading event) are thought to aggravate water quality deterioration due to large flushes of accumulated contaminants from urban surfaces into water bodies. This study evaluates the link between these cascading events and surface water quality. For this purpose, the study identifies and characterises the impact of individual rain events on surface water quality at nine urban water bodies using high-resolution rain and water quality data over a period of 10–20 years. To analyse the cascade and its resulting water quality impact, the study compares two definitions for deriving antecedent dry spell length of a rain event: a classic definition based on a daily rainfall threshold of 1 mm and a new definition based on events' wash-off potential. SWMM is used in the new definition as a signal-processing tool to derive pollution accumulation and wash-off calculated using 1-min rainfall series. The comparison shows a clear difference in the resulting dry spell length–rain–impact relationships. The classic definition—useful for understanding meteorological dryness—tends to oversimplify pollution accumulation and transport wash off, and thereby heavily undermines the importance of dry spell length or cascade. However, the new definition incorporates additional process details relevant for pollutant buildup, rainfall–runoff and wash-off potential, making it more suitable for linking cascading events to surface water quality. Furthermore, this study evaluates the importance of antecedent dry period on the impact on receiving water quality. The findings demonstrate that, in most cases, the impact on surface water quality is heavily influenced by antecedent dry spell length along with rain characteristics. The importance of cascading events emphasises the need to implement source control methods to minimise the effects of long dry spells and resulting pollution accumulation on urban surfaces thus causing diffuse pollution.
